title: Lesson Plan — Units, Dimensions and Vectors (Class 12 NIOS Physics)
subject: Physics
objectives: State the seven SI base units and identify common derived units (N, J, W, Pa, Hz) in terms of base units.
Write the dimensional formula of a given quantity and apply the principle of homogeneity to check the consistency of an equation.
Compute mean absolute, relative and percentage errors and apply the rules for combining errors in sums, products and powers.
Distinguish scalars from vectors and resolve a vector into Cartesian components.
Compute scalar (dot) and vector (cross) products and apply them to find work done and torque.
prerequisites: Class 11 idea of speed, distance, time, force.
Comfort with basic algebra and trigonometry (sin, cos at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°).
Familiarity with scientific notation and logarithms.
materials: A4 'SI base units + dimensions' reference sheet (one per pair)
Vernier calliper or screw gauge for a quick measurement demo
Set of arrow cards (printed vectors of various magnitudes and directions) for the addition activity
Calculator (one per pair) for error and component arithmetic
Worksheet handout (Worksheet — Units, Dimensions and Vectors)

activities.description: Quick measurement demo: the teacher measures the diameter of a coin three times with a Vernier calliper, recording slightly different values each time. Asks the class: 'Which value is the right one? How do we report this?' Sets up the need for error analysis later in the lesson.
teacher_actions: Demo three Vernier calliper readings of the same coin.
Write the three values on the board; collect student suggestions for the 'best' value.
Promise the rule for handling this is in the Significant Figures / Errors section later.
student_actions: Compute the mean as a quick sanity step.
Note their suggestion for how to report uncertainty.

activities.description: Pair card sort: students receive a stack of unit cards (m/s, N, J·s, kg·m/s², kg·m²/s²) and a list of physical quantities (velocity, force, momentum, energy, action). They match each unit to the right physical quantity. Mismatches surface the value of dimensional analysis.
teacher_actions: Distribute card stacks; give pairs 8 minutes.
Listen for confusions between energy and momentum; J·s and kg·m/s².
Pick two pairs to share their reasoning.
student_actions: Match cards collaboratively; argue when uncertain.
Tag any card-pair they disagreed about for the Explain phase.

activities.description: Direct instruction: the teacher (i) lists the seven SI base units and works through how derived units come from them; (ii) builds the dimensional formulas for velocity, acceleration, force, energy, power and pressure on the board; (iii) shows two worked examples — a consistency check on v² = u² + 2as and a derivation of T ∝ √(L/g) for a pendulum; (iv) covers significant-figure rules and error propagation; (v) introduces vectors with arrow diagrams and resolves a 10-N force at 60° into components.
teacher_actions: Build a 'reference card' on the board: 7 base units + 5 dimensional formulas + sig-fig rules.
Long-derive T ∝ √(L/g) live; ask students to call out each step.
Resolve a 10-N force at 60° into components on the board.
Draw two arrows for the parallelogram-law demo.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate each worked example in their notebooks.
Predict the dimensional formula of pressure before the teacher writes it.
Add the sig-fig rules and the dot/cross-product formulas to a 'rules box' for quick reference.

activities.description: Application station: students work through six problems — two on dimensional analysis (one consistency check, one formula derivation), one on percentage error propagation, two on vector addition / component resolution, and one on a dot product / work calculation. The teacher circulates and prompts students who get stuck to verbalise their first step.
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a student.
Collect common mistakes for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Solve the six problems individually, showing all steps.
Self-check against a posted answer key after the first three.
Ask a peer before asking the teacher.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: an 8-question MCQ + short-answer slip with at least one item per content area, drawn from the chapter's question bank. Students complete it silently in 9 minutes; the teacher then projects the answers and runs a 4-minute discussion focused on the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute the exit-ticket; remind students it is individual work.
Time the quiz to 9 minutes strictly.
Quickly tally results and address the top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection on the item they got wrong, if any.

activities.description: Set homework: complete the rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE-level prompt from the bank ('Construct a single equation involving force F, mass m, velocity v, and time t that is dimensionally consistent, and verify the consistency'). Preview the next chapter (Motion in a Straight Line) by writing v = u + at on the board and asking students to predict its dimensional consistency.
teacher_actions: Announce homework due date and the CREATE prompt.
Bridge to the next chapter with v = u + at.
student_actions: Pack the worksheet for home study.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Units, Dimensions and Vectors handout.
Complete one CREATE-level prompt from the question bank: invent an equation involving force, mass, velocity and time that is dimensionally consistent, and verify.
Find three measurements from the textbook (e.g. mass of an electron, speed of light, Avogadro's number) and write each in scientific notation with the correct number of significant figures.
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket described in the Evaluate phase as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question MCQ + 2 long-answer quiz drawn from the chapter's question bank for the next class as a summative assessment.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on three-vector subtraction (\vec{a} − \vec{b}, dot, cross product) using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a simple two-criterion rubric (dimensionally consistent? algebra correct?).
references: NIOS Senior Secondary Physics, Module 1, Lesson 1: Units, Dimensions and Vectors.
NCERT Class 11 Physics, Chapter 2: Units and Measurements; Chapter 4: Motion in a Plane (vector treatment).
